experiment.name: Meta experiment: a final review of all 23 experiments for research leads on severe canine babesiosis
experiment.description: Does any result of the 23 experiments, alone or in agreement across independent sources, point to a severity correlate, a mechanism or a human-disease parallel worth further research? Hypothesis-generating: every candidate is screened, checked for novelty and given a separate refutation attempt before it is tiered.
experiment.summary: 0 candidates reached tier A, 0 tier B, 1 tier C, 6 tier D and 22 were rejected (X), out of 29 candidates. No candidate reached tier A or B: no single result is a new, non-circular severity finding. The strongest convergent theme that is not a known driver is the monocyte theme (T02: circulating monocyte count, with CD14 and CCL2): 4 of 4 B. rossi sources in the expected direction, Stouffer Z 3.94, BH q 0.00016 over 8 themes, leave-one-source-out max p 0.011. 8 B. rossi theme tests, 4 with BH q < 0.05 (two of them known drivers: neutrophils and anaemia; one fails leave-one-source-out).

payload.answer: 0 candidates reached tier A, 0 tier B, 1 tier C, 6 tier D and 22 were rejected (X), out of 29 candidates. No candidate reached tier A or B: no single result is a new, non-circular severity finding. Tier C (convergent across independent sources): Higher circulating monocyte count in more severe disease (with CD14 and CCL2 as supporting markers). Tier D (gaps with strong human evidence and a canine assay): Intravascular haemolysis per unit of anaemia (cell-free haemoglobin, haem scavenging); Neutrophil degranulation and extracellular traps (NETs, histones, released MPO and elastase, calprotectin); Angiopoietin-2 and the Ang-2/Ang-1 ratio; VWF, ultra-large multimers and ADAMTS13; Ferritin (hyperferritinaemia); Kynurenine pathway (kynurenine:tryptophan).

A lead is a thing to measure, not a predictor. Died includes euthanasia in the Onderstepoort files. One species per source: between-file differences are not species effects.

payload.hypothesis: In B. rossi babesiosis, a higher circulating monocyte count at admission goes with more severe disease, beyond anaemia and total leukocytes.
payload.evidence: T02: 4 of 4 B. rossi sources in the expected direction (DS05 monocytes with dullness rho +0.45, partial +0.29 after haematocrit, WBC, segmented and band neutrophils and illness days; S-CB517 died +0.25; DS07 CD14 +0.42, halves after haemoglobin beta; Beagles +0.67), Stouffer q 0.00016 over 8 themes; but without DS05, the source that suggested it, Z 2.31 (Bonferroni 0.084). Monocyte count does not track MCP-1
payload.human_counterpart: Monocyte/macrophage markers with severity: soluble CD14 with severity in falciparum malaria and presepsin (sCD14-ST) higher in sepsis non-survivors agree; MCP-1 independently prognostic in sepsis; but monocyte activation markers were lower in severe malaria in Malawian children and MCP-1 lower in complicated falciparum malaria (mixed)
payload.parallel_new: partly: the CCL2 (MCP-1) parallel is made in CB017, CB517, CB107; a circulating monocyte count or sCD14 parallel was not found in a CB text
payload.refuted_by: No monocyte-count difference by outcome in a non-Onderstepoort B. rossi cohort with a hard outcome, or a difference that disappears after WBC and haematocrit adjustment
payload.next_existing: Monocyte count and monocyte fraction against death in the probable DS03-S-CB050 join is not possible (DS03 has no leukocytes); cheapest: ask the CB040 authors (320 B. rossi dogs, SV-02c request) for dog-level monocyte counts and outcome
payload.next_new_dogs: SV-10-03 prospective B. rossi cohort with at least 200 dogs outside Onderstepoort: admission CBC with differential, outcome components stored separately
payload.minimum_dataset: Manual or analyser differential with absolute monocyte count; plasma sCD14 (presepsin) and CCL2 on stored pre-treatment plasma

payload.hypothesis: Neutrophil degranulation and extracellular trap release (cfDNA, nucleosomes, histones, released MPO and elastase, calprotectin) are greater in severe B. rossi babesiosis, beyond neutrophil number.
payload.evidence: Gap: never measured in canine babesiosis (CB107 states NETosis is unstudied). Weak, confounded support: DS07 S100A8 +0.43 (q 0.29), a third explained by haemoglobin beta; histone H4 untestable; Beagle granule transcripts rose in all 5 dogs with no severity gradient
payload.human_counterpart: Plasma elastase and MPO higher in cerebral malaria; circulating histones raised with brain swelling in cerebral malaria; neutrophil granule transcripts associated with severe malaria and with sepsis mortality; but cfDNA and MPO-DNA did not predict death after adjustment in a sepsis cohort (mixed)
payload.parallel_new: yes for NETs, histones, calprotectin and released MPO/elastase (only speculated in CB articles); band neutrophils and MPXI are published
payload.refuted_by: Plasma cfDNA, nucleosomes or calprotectin no higher in dogs that die once the band neutrophil count is adjusted for
payload.next_existing: Re-quantify DS06 from SRA PRJNA703846 without the CPM filter to recover MPO and ELANE (a coordinator decision, large download); no severity contrast in those 5 dogs
payload.next_new_dogs: SV-10-03 cohort: citrate plasma (not serum) for cfDNA by fluorometry and calprotectin; nucleosome ELISA only with a haemolysis and icterus check
payload.minimum_dataset: Plasma cfDNA, calprotectin (S100A8/A9), plasma MPO and elastase; band and segmented neutrophil counts
payload.canine_line: Never measured in canine babesiosis. Nearest data: DS07 S100A8 +0.43 (q 0.29) and a Beagle granule-transcript rise with no severity gradient

human.claim: Plasma neutrophil elastase, MPO and proteinase 3 (not lactoferrin or lipocalin) higher in retinopathy-positive paediatric cerebral malaria; neutrophil transcripts most upregulated; but no NETs found in brain autopsy micr
In 341 ICU patients an ex vivo NET-forming assay predicted DIC and death independently of APACHE II, whereas cfDNA, MPO and MPO-DNA complexes did not (HU008)
Circulating extracellular histones, about equally host and parasite origin, are raised in paediatric cerebral malaria and associated with brain swelling (HU021)
Whole-blood neutrophil degranulation genes (ELANE, MPO, PRTN3, CEACAM8, DEFA4) higher in 30-day sepsis non-survivors after adjustment for neutrophil count, replicated in a second cohort (HU006)

Neutrophil granule gene expression associated with all severe malaria phenotypes in Gambian children, but up to 99 percent of host differential expression was driven by parasite load (Lee et al. 2018)

payload.label: Higher circulating monocyte count in more severe disease (with CD14 and CCL2 as supporting markers)
payload.evidence: T02 B. rossi 4 of 4 sources in the expected direction, Stouffer one-sided p 4e-05, BH q 0.00016 over 8 themes (themes chosen after results were seen), leave-one-source-out max p 0.0105; with SRC-D 5 of 5
payload.novelty_where: CCL2 by outcome published per cohort (CB517, CB017); CD14 by complicated status (CB112); monocyte activation proposed as a mechanism (CB107, CB119, CB517); CCL2 also published in an independent B. rossi cohort (CB037). No CB article combines independent sources, and the DS05 (Eastern Cape) monocyte association is unpublished. The sCD14/presepsin parallel is not made in a CB text found
payload.refutation_reason: No single check rejects the lead. The DS05 monocyte-dullness association survives adjustment for haematocrit, total and differential leukocytes and illness days (partial rho about +0.28), and the post hoc marker choice was conservative. But the cross-source support outside the source that suggested it is weak: without SRC-F, Z 2.31, Bonferroni over 8 themes 0.084. In the two hard-outcome sources the monocyte difference is no larger than the WBC difference, and half of the DS07 CD14 signal goes with haemoglobin beta. Monocyte count does not track MCP-1, the CCL2 form is already published (CB107, CB517, CB037, CB017), and the only direct activation marker in B. rossi (CB504) points the other way in non-survivors.

payload.label: Inflammation against regeneration at a given haematocrit (SV-09 residual axis 2) tracks dullness
payload.evidence: partial rho with habitus -0.26 (-0.40 to -0.10), p 0.003, family of 2 axes, n 140 (DS05, already seen: exploratory)
payload.novelty_where: inadequate regeneration and cytokine-suppressed erythropoiesis proposed in CB115, CB129, CB082, with the malaria parallel (CB129, CB115); no CB article links it to clinical severity
payload.refutation_reason: The axis-2 association with habitus does not survive control for band neutrophils and monocytes (rho -0.10, -0.27 to +0.07), so it restates leukocytes already known to track dullness, a known driver under the spec. The named mechanism is also absent: at a given haematocrit the leukocyte and regeneration sides are uncorrelated (rho -0.002) and leukocytes do not go with lower ARC. What remains is a weak, uncorrected ARC-brighter link (rho +0.18, p 0.03) in one already-seen clinic file, which could be re-entered as a separate gap/test lead (the DS03-S-CB050 join) but not as K02.

payload.label: Intravascular haemolysis per unit of anaemia (cell-free haemoglobin, haem scavenging)
payload.evidence: T04: DS07 haemoglobin beta +0.48 (+0.09 to +0.82), q 0.133; DS02 cfHb change high vs low dose +1.0 (exact p 0.2); Stouffer p 0.005, q 0.010, leave-one-source-out fails (max p 0.1), so not tier C
payload.novelty_where: SV-06a F1-01 measured_no_severity (CB082, CB412); haem oxygenase-1 never measured; haemopexin and haptoglobin measured without severity
payload.refutation_reason: The gap stands: no CB article relates measured cell-free haemoglobin or haem load to outcome in natural canine babesiosis, the human evidence (falciparum, knowlesi, sepsis) agrees, and canine assays exist. The programme's 'weak convergent support' does not hold. DS02 is a pure parasite-load effect that CB082 already reports. DS07 haemoglobin beta partly restates the label, cannot be put per unit of anaemia, moves with another red-cell protein (sample haemolysis not excluded), drops below significance when adjusted for lactoferrin or CD14 or when the top 3 dogs are removed, and has q 0.133. So T04 should be cited as a literature gap, not as a data signal.

payload.label: Neutrophil degranulation and extracellular traps (NETs, histones, released MPO and elastase, calprotectin)
payload.evidence: SV-08 neutrophil-granule score rose in 5 of 5 Beagles (also in mild dogs; MPO, ELANE missing); DS07 S100A8 +0.43 (-0.10 to +0.93), q 0.29; histone H4 untestable
payload.novelty_where: SV-06a ranks 3, 4, 5, 9: never measured in canine babesiosis; band neutrophils and MPXI are published (CB050, CB040)
payload.refutation_reason: The gap is real: no study has measured NETs, cfDNA, nucleosomes, circulating histones, calprotectin or released MPO/elastase against severity or outcome in canine babesiosis, and CB107 states NETosis is unstudied. The canine support is weak and confounded: no signal passes correction (S100A8 q 0.29, H4 untestable), half the lactoferrin and a third of the S100A8 effect go with serum haemoglobin, the DS07 label contains band neutrophils, and SV-08 shows a response to infection with no severity gradient that tracks band counts. It remains a literature-driven gap lead, not a data-supported finding, and the human evidence itself is mixed.

payload.label: Angiopoietin-2 and the Ang-2/Ang-1 ratio
payload.evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (6 human cohorts), validated canine assay
payload.novelty_where: SV-06a rank 1, never measured in canine babesiosis
payload.refutation_reason: No canine babesiosis study has measured angiopoietin-2, the human severity evidence is strong (systematic review of 11 falciparum studies, sepsis meta-analysis of 33 studies) and a validated canine Ang-2 ELISA exists with prognostic data in canine sepsis. The candidate is weakened only because Ang-1 could not be measured with the validated kit, so the Ang-2/Ang-1 ratio is not assayable in dogs; the lead should be restricted to Ang-2 and adjusted for haemolysis and creatinine.

payload.label: VWF, ultra-large multimers and ADAMTS13
payload.evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine assay
payload.novelty_where: SV-06a rank 6, measured only against controls (CB446)
payload.refutation_reason: No canine babesiosis study has measured VWF or ADAMTS13 against severity or outcome, and CB145, the obvious threat, measured factor activities but not VWF or ADAMTS13. Validated canine assays exist for both. The lead is weakened because the human VWF/ADAMTS13 ratio evidence rests largely on one small cohort and because the single canine measurement (CB446) found vWF activity lower, not higher, than in controls, so the direction of transfer cannot be assumed.

payload.label: VEGF and soluble VEGFR-1 (sFlt-1)
payload.evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine VEGF assay
payload.novelty_where: SV-06a rank 2, never measured
payload.refutation_reason: The gap itself is real: no canine babesiosis study has measured VEGF or sFlt-1, and CB122 only names VEGF as an enriched pathway. But the tier D rule fails on the other two conditions at once. The human severity evidence is grade 2 at best and inconsistent in direction for VEGF (protective in cerebral malaria, raised in uncomplicated malaria, low with immunosuppression in human babesiosis), while the stronger sepsis sFlt-1 evidence rests on one cohort; and no canine sFlt-1 assay exists, so the half with the better human case cannot be measured in dogs at all.

payload.label: Ferritin (hyperferritinaemia)
payload.evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine assay
payload.novelty_where: SV-06a rank 7, measured, no difference 7 vs 7 (CB242)
payload.refutation_reason: Ferritin has never been measured against severity or outcome in canine babesiosis: the only measurement (CB242, 7 vs 7, infected versus healthy, no difference) has no severity contrast and no power, and CB132 is a single severe case with hyperferritinaemia. The human sepsis evidence is strong across three cohorts, and canine ferritin assays are in use. The lead is weakened because the malaria evidence is an infection contrast rather than a severity one, because no formal canine assay validation was found, and because ferritin in a haemolytic disease is heavily confounded by haemolysis and the acute-phase response.

payload.label: Kynurenine pathway (kynurenine:tryptophan)
payload.evidence: SV-06a grade 3 (4 human cohorts), validated canine assay
payload.novelty_where: SV-06a rank 8, measured against controls in B. canis (CB091)
payload.refutation_reason: No canine babesiosis study has measured the kynurenine pathway against severity or outcome; CB091 is an infected-versus-healthy contrast, which my re-analysis of its supplement confirms is large (Kyn/Trp delta +0.86, p 3.8e-04). The human sepsis and critical-illness evidence is strong across several cohorts and a validated canine plasma LC-MS/MS assay exists, so tier D holds. It is weakened because the nearest severity proxy that can be computed now, the CB071 renal-function groups, shows no urinary kynurenine or tryptophan difference, because the malaria evidence is mostly CSF and cerebral, and because kynurenine is confounded by azotaemia and by inflammatory intensity.

payload.result: Unadjusted rho +0.448 (p 1.3e-08, n 147). Partial on haematocrit +0.28 (+0.11 to +0.42, p 0.0006); on WBC +0.38 (p 2.9e-06); on segmented neutrophils +0.42; on band neutrophils +0.33 (p 5.6e-05); on illness days +0.45; on haematocrit + WBC +0.32 (p 9.5e-05); on haematocrit + segs + bands +0.26 (p 0.0016); on all five +0.29 (+0.13 to +0.44, p 0.0006, n 145); adding lymphocytes, platelets and temperature +0.28 (p 0.0009, n 141). Anaemia explains about a third of the association (haematocrit with dullness rho -0.53; monocytes with haematocrit -0.44), but it does not remove it.

payload.reason_tested: general leukocytosis rather than monocytes (specificity, SRC-F)
payload.result: WBC rho +0.27, segs +0.19, lymphocytes +0.20, bands +0.38 with dullness. After partialling monocytes: WBC -0.04 (p 0.66), segs -0.06, lymphocytes +0.01, bands +0.20 (p 0.015). Monocyte fraction of WBC with dullness +0.33 (p 5.7e-05). In DS05 the monocyte count carries the leukocyte signal, not the other way round.

payload.reason_tested: co-infection and outliers in SRC-F
payload.result: Without E. canis: rho +0.453 (n 144). Without top 5% monocytes: +0.422 (n 139). Dull >= 2 vs < 2: Cliff +0.55 (+0.39 to +0.68), p 0.0001. Only 10 dogs were BAR, so 'any dullness' compares 137 with 10 (Cliff +0.38, p 0.039).

payload.reason_tested: hard-outcome sources: effect not beyond total leukocytes; label partly contains leukocytes
payload.result: SRC-A: monocyte count Cliff +0.25 (-0.18 to +0.63, p 0.17; medians 0.81 vs 0.52); WBC +0.22 (p 0.23); monocyte fraction +0.11 (-0.28 to +0.46, p 0.53); WBC-adjusted +0.19 (p 0.30). SRC-D: monocyte count +0.23 (p 0.24), WBC +0.23, monocyte % -0.01 (-0.41 to +0.38, p 0.96), WBC-adjusted +0.17 (p 0.43). The SRC-D 'complicated' label requires SIRS, of which WBC is a criterion. In both sources with a hard or clinical outcome the monocyte difference is no larger than the total-leukocyte difference, and neither interval excludes 0.

payload.reason_tested: contradiction: CB504 fewer P-selectin-positive monocytes in non-survivors
payload.result: CB504 (DOI 10.1016/j.tvjl.2015.05.008): CD62P-positive monocytes 58.9% in 29 survivors, 39.2% in 7 non-survivors (no significant difference), survivors above controls (35.3%) and non-survivors not. Same cohort as SRC-A (CH03, Onderstepoort Oct 2011 - Apr 2013), so probably overlapping dogs. The marker is platelet-monocyte aggregation, not monocyte number, and the comparison is underpowered, so it does not reject a count claim. It does contradict the word 'activation': the one direct cellular activation marker measured in B. rossi points the other way in non-survivors, as do monocyte activation markers in Malawian children with severe malaria (10.1111/pim.12319).

payload.reason_tested: construct validity: monocyte count, MCP-1 and serum CD14 are not one measure
payload.result: SRC-A rho -0.17 (p 0.09, n 97); SRC-D +0.20 (p 0.28, n 31). CB517 itself remarks on the absence of monocytosis despite high MCP-1. The theme combines a circulating count, a chemokine and a serum receptor protein that do not co-vary, so the combined Z supports 'several monocyte-lineage indicators lean the same way', not one 'activation' process.

payload.reason_tested: assay/sample artefact: DS07 CD14 confounded with haemoglobin beta (haemolysis)
payload.result: CD14 vs HBB rho +0.46 (p 0.008, n 32; within complicated +0.58, within uncomplicated +0.13). CD14 complicated vs uncomplicated: unadjusted Cliff +0.42 (+0.04 to +0.75, p 0.044); HBB-adjusted +0.24 (-0.18 to +0.63, p 0.27); partial r +0.22 (p 0.25); plex-centred +0.39 (p 0.062). HBB itself +0.48 (p 0.022), and the label contains haematocrit < 0.15. About half the CD14 signal goes with the haemoglobin signal; in-vivo haemolysis, anaemia severity and stored-sample haemolysis cannot be separated. Replacing SRC-C with the adjusted value: 4-source Z 3.60 (p 0.00016); without SRC-F Z 1.91 (p 0.028).

payload.reason_tested: same dogs counted twice (SV-07)
payload.result: T02 uses S-CB517 (S-CB050 cohort 1, 2011-2013) for SRC-A. The unverified DS07 overlap runs through DS04 to S-CB050 cohort 2 (2014; cases 126, 127, 131), which are not S-CB517 dogs. SRC-B are experimental Beagles, SRC-F is an Eastern Cape clinic in 2021, SRC-D is Zagreb. No dog is counted twice among the T02 indicators. CB504 (not an indicator) is probably the same dogs as SRC-A.

payload.reason_tested: post hoc choice of monocyte count over MCP-1
payload.result: With SRC-F: Z 3.94 (count, count) to 4.80 (MCP-1, MCP-1). Without SRC-F: Z 2.31 to 3.29. The count is the most conservative choice, so the choice did not inflate the result.

payload.reason_tested: correction for themes; dependence on the hypothesis-generating source
payload.result: SRC-F generated the idea (EXP01) and carries the combination; its p is a permutation floor (1e-4; analytic p 1.3e-08). Without SRC-F: Z 2.31, p 0.0105, Bonferroni over 8 themes 0.084. Without SRC-F and SRC-C (the CB112 positive control): Z 1.56, p 0.060. Monocyte count alone in sources other than SRC-F (A, B): Z 1.56, p 0.060. The spec screen (BH q 0.00016, every leave-one-out p < 0.05) is met, but the replication evidence outside the source that suggested it does not survive the theme correction.

payload.reason_tested: already published in a CB article
payload.result: MCP-1 with severity is published in B. rossi by CB517 (non-survivors, 10.1371/journal.pone.0150113) and CB037 (critically ill and non-survivors, independent cohort), and in B. canis by CB017 (complicated, 10.1371/journal.pone.0190474). CB112 (10.1038/s41598-023-37312-9) reports higher CD14 in complicated dogs. CB107 (2023 review) combines the B. rossi and B. canis CCL2 findings and states that they indicate classical monocyte activation in severe canine babesiosis. CB119, CB129 and CB147 describe monocyte-macrophage expansion in tissues of fatal B. rossi cases. The cross-source CCL2 form of the claim (T02s) is therefore already published. The circulating-monocyte-count form is not: CB517 reported no monocyte difference by outcome, CB126 (the DS05 article) did not relate monocytes to habitus, and CB098 reports monocyte differences by dose, not by severity.

payload.reason_tested: marker in the severity label; weak sources
payload.result: DS05 habitus does not contain any leukocyte value. The DS07 label contains band neutrophils and haematocrit, not CD14. The S-CB017 label contains SIRS (WBC), which partly contains monocyte count (see the hard-outcome attempt). SRC-B compares dose (3 vs 2 Beagles, minimum exact two-sided p 0.2), not severity, but it gets equal weight in the Stouffer combination.

payload.reason_tested: known driver: the axis restates band neutrophils and monocytes
payload.result: Reproduced SV-09: rho -0.257 (-0.408 to -0.097), p 0.002, n 140. Adding bands: -0.167 (-0.313 to -0.003), p 0.049. Adding bands and monocytes: -0.100 (-0.265 to +0.071), p 0.24. Adding all four leukocyte types: -0.130 (-0.280 to +0.018), p 0.12. Total WBC does not explain it (-0.240, p 0.005). Bands alone at a given haematocrit -0.270 (p 0.0008) and monocytes alone -0.276 (p 0.002) are each as strong as the whole axis. The axis-2 link with habitus does not survive control for the two leukocytes already known to track habitus.

payload.reason_tested: regeneration side alone
payload.result: Singles: ARC +0.176 (+0.009 to +0.343), p 0.034; reticulocyte % +0.186, p 0.026 (more reticulocytes, brighter); MCV +0.03, RDW +0.07, MCHC -0.13 (p 0.11), nRBC -0.12: none of these passes. Regeneration side composite -0.170 (-0.315 to -0.019), p 0.042; without MCHC -0.174, p 0.037; after bands and monocytes -0.171 to -0.195, p 0.017 to 0.043. A weak, nominal residual signal that is independent of leukocytes, carried by ARC. It would not pass BH over the census family or over the four checks in this attempt (smallest q about 0.07).

payload.reason_tested: mechanism: is more inflammation coupled with less regeneration?
payload.result: Leukocyte side vs regeneration side rho -0.002. Unweighted leukocyte sum vs ARC +0.033 (-0.141 to +0.209); vs ARC plus RDW +0.111 (-0.070 to +0.292). Bands vs ARC +0.04; monocytes vs ARC -0.13 (-0.30 to +0.04); segmented vs RDW +0.28 (+0.11 to +0.46). Product term vs habitus +0.079, p 0.34. At a given haematocrit, dogs with more inflammatory leukocytes do not have less regeneration; axis 2 is a contrast created by orthogonality to axis 1 (which moves leukocytes and regeneration together). The named mechanism, inflammation-suppressed regeneration between dogs, is not present in these data; the axis is two independent weak correlates of habitus added together.

payload.reason_tested: assay artefact: MCHC and reticulocyte arithmetic, haemoglobinaemia
payload.result: Residual MCHC vs ARC -0.41 and vs MCV -0.46: the largest loading (MCHC 0.66) is in part the arithmetic of large, low-MCHC reticulocytes, and calculated MCHC is also raised by free plasma haemoglobin in intravascular haemolysis (not measured in DS05, so not separable). Removing MCHC barely changes the habitus link (axis after MCHC -0.224, p 0.006; regeneration side without MCHC -0.174). Artefact explains the axis shape, not the habitus association.

payload.reason_tested: confounding: co-infection, illness duration, habitus coding, outliers, fever
payload.result: No E. canis: -0.258, p 0.003 (n 137). Illness class plus days: -0.266, p 0.003. Illness <= 7 days: -0.268, p 0.002 (n 132; only 8 dogs > 7 days). No collapsed dogs: -0.259, p 0.003. Bright (4+, n 9) vs not: -0.170, p 0.036. Trimmed 5%: -0.210, p 0.018. Temperature: -0.242, p 0.005. Not an artefact of co-infection, duration, fever or a few dogs; direction stable.

payload.reason_tested: already published in a CB article
payload.result: No CB article reports ARC or a leukocyte-against-regeneration balance against habitus or outcome in B. rossi. CB040 (10.1016/j.vetpar.2019.06.005; 320 B. rossi dogs) reports poor regeneration (ARC < 100 in about 62%) but no ARC-outcome test. CB115 (10.1111/vcp.13228) compares ARC with IMHA and controls and over time in experimental dogs (ARC falls about 48 h after parasitaemia), no severity contrast. CB082 (10.1186/s12864-021-07889-4; experimental B. rossi) notes reticulocytosis suppressed as parasitaemia climbed. CB129 (10.36303/jsava.626) shows dyserythropoiesis in marrow. CB074 (B. gibsoni, abstract only) reports reticulocytes correlated with survival (different species, direction not given in abstract). CB126, the article on the DS05 dogs, does not analyse habitus. Not published as a B. rossi severity finding; the mechanism parallel is already made (CB115, CB129).

payload.reason_tested: tier B eligibility under SV-META spec section 8
payload.result: Tier B needs a screen pass in one source that is not circular and not a known driver (restates anaemia, band neutrophils or the label). The axis-2 association is a known driver by this test (it vanishes after bands and monocytes). It is one source (SRC-F), already-seen data, with an outcome (habitus) that is soft and owner/clinician graded; the SV-09-03 hard-outcome test restated band neutrophils. The surviving piece (ARC at a given haematocrit with habitus, rho +0.18, p 0.03) is computed here, outside any declared family, and would not pass BH over the census family. Neither part meets tier B.

payload.reason_tested: marker is in the severity label / confounded by anaemia (DS07)
payload.result: Reproduced: Cliff +0.476, within-plex permutation p 0.02, bootstrap 95% CI +0.09 to +0.81 (14 vs 18). DS07 has no haematocrit, bilirubin or haemolysis index, so haemoglobin beta cannot be expressed 'per unit of anaemia'; the candidate's central quantity is not measured in either source. The label contains haematocrit < 0.15 and bilirubin > 30, both haemolysis consequences, so a dog can be 'complicated' because it haemolysed more; the contrast is partly circular. Uncomplicated infected dogs equal healthy controls (Cliff -0.006), although all B. rossi dogs haemolyse. Not a formal rejection alone because the label variables are not in the file, but it removes the 'per unit of anaemia' interpretation.

payload.reason_tested: sample (ex vivo) haemolysis or a shared pre-analytical factor (DS07)
payload.result: PRDX2 is also higher in complicated dogs (Cliff +0.74, p 0.006, 9 vs 13) and moves with haemoglobin beta (rho +0.77); the HBB/PRDX2 ratio does not differ (Cliff +0.16, p 0.45). A real test needs stored serum or plasma with a hard outcome, which means the Onderstepoort B. rossi material.

sections.heading: Question
paragraphs: Does any result of the 23 experiments, alone or across independent sources, point to a severity correlate, a new mechanism or a human-disease parallel worth further research?

sections.heading: What was done
paragraphs: 495 results were read from the package files and screened (39 pass the statistical screen). Fifteen themes were scored with one indicator per independent source and combined over 8 themes; each surviving candidate got a separate refutation attempt by a sub-agent (9 candidates, 62 checks).

sections.heading: Result
paragraphs: 0 candidates reached tier A, 0 tier B, 1 tier C, 6 tier D and 22 were rejected (X), out of 29 candidates. No candidate reached tier A or B: no single result is a new, non-circular severity finding.
The monocyte lead (tier C) agrees in 4 of 4 B. rossi sources (BH q 0.00016) but rests mostly on DS05, the file that suggested it. Tier D leads have no canine severity data.

sections.heading: What this does not show
paragraphs: No lead is a confirmed finding or a predictor: the files were already seen and the themes were chosen afterwards. Died includes euthanasia (Onderstepoort); one species per source.
